heroHeadline: Huawei Accelerates Ascend 960 AI Chip to Q1 2027 as Beijing Rejects Anthropic's AI-Slowdown Call Ahead of Xi's Washington Visit
heroSubtitle: September 18, 2026 — Two developments this week frame China's domestic AI posture days before Xi Jinping's planned September 24 Washington visit. On September 14, Foreign Ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun rejected an essay Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei published September 12 warning of a 'Chinese lead in AI' and urging continued chip export restrictions, calling it 'fearmongering, confrontation and vicious competition' — state-run China Daily followed September 15 accusing US AI executives of a 'self-serving' push to blunt Chinese competition via safety rhetoric now that hardware curbs have failed to stop competitive Chinese models. On September 17 at Huawei Connect 2026 in Shanghai, rotating chairman David Wang pulled the Ascend 960DT AI training chip's commercial launch forward to Q1 2027 — three quarters ahead of schedule — and unveiled the Atlas 960 SuperPoD, a 4,096-card Near-Packaged-Optics cluster delivering up to 8 exaflops of FP8 compute and 1 petabyte of HBM, while previewing an annual Ascend cadence through 2029. Together the week shows Beijing pairing a firm diplomatic rebuttal of Western AI-safety framing with a public hardware roadmap accelerating faster than export-control skeptics expected, both timed to land just ahead of the Trump-Xi summit.
